primary_diagnosis: End-stage renal disease (dialysis-naïve) secondary to diabetic nephropathy and hypertensive nephrosclerosis
clinical_reasoning_summary: The patient meets ESRD criteria (eGFR 6 mL/min/1.73 m²) in the context of longstanding diabetes and hypertension, making dialysis‑naïve ESRD the dominant diagnosis. Cardiovascular disease, hypoglycemia risk, CKD‑MBD, anemia, occult GI bleeding, possible HFpEF, and psychosocial barriers are recognized comorbidities with probabilities adjusted per reviewer confidence. Gaps in laboratory data, medication reconciliation, and cardiac imaging limit certainty for several secondary diagnoses.
unresolved_findings: Very dilute urine specific gravity 1.0 (could suggest diabetes insipidus or excessive fluid intake beyond CKD expectations)
Absence of recent vital signs, lipid panel, and repeat renal labs (last visit documented in 2001)
Potential medication gaps (no explicit list of ACE‑I/ARB, NSAIDs, ESA, phosphate binders, statin, antiplatelet agents)
No documented dialysis initiation despite eGFR 6 mL/min/1.73 m²
recommended_workup: Formal dialysis eligibility assessment and discussion of initiation timing
Comprehensive CKD-MBD panel: serum calcium, phosphate, PTH, 25‑OH vitamin D
Iron studies (ferritin, transferrin saturation) to delineate anemia etiology
Review and reconcile current medication list, ensure renin‑angiotensin system blockade and anemia management
Cardiac evaluation: ECG and transthoracic echocardiogram to assess for HFpEF or ischemia
Stress testing or coronary imaging if angina symptoms persist
Repeat fecal occult blood test and consider upper/lower endoscopy for GI bleed source
Structured psychosocial assessment (social work, transplant counseling) to address adherence barriers
Urine osmolality and water balance studies to investigate dilute urine finding
